# chia.vlsi.sram_openram — OpenRAM SRAM macros for synthesis

Drop-in alternative to `chia.vlsi.sram_cacti`: instead of a CACTI estimate
wrapped in a chia-generated Liberty/LEF, every SRAM in a Chipyard design gets a
**real sky130 macro** generated by the [OpenRAM](https://github.com/VLSIDA/OpenRAM)
compiler, and synthesis consumes OpenRAM's **native** Liberty (one per corner),
LEF and Verilog model untouched.

| | CACTI (`sram_cacti`) | OpenRAM (`sram_openram`) |
|---|---|---|
| per-macro cost | milliseconds | minutes to hours (layout generation) |
| collateral | chia-generated Liberty/LEF (Chipyard pin names) | OpenRAM's own `.lib`/`.lef`/`.v` |
| read timing | `rising_edge` clk→q = access time | **`falling_edge`**: data valid half a cycle plus the access delay after the capturing edge |
| macro per | Chipyard SRAM | geometry (`openram_sky130_1rw_2048x64_m8`); identical geometries share one macro |
| glue | blackbox stub | per-SRAM Verilog **adapter** (`openram_<sram>`) + macro blackbox stub |
| unsupported shapes | analytical fallback | **error** (3+ ports, read-/write-only); no fallback |
| results | recomputed every time | content-addressed **cache** on the worker node |
| Ray resource | `cacti` | `openram` (image `ghcr.io/ucb-bar/chia-openram`) |

## Entry points (same shape as `sram_cacti`)

```python
from chia.vlsi.sram_openram.sram_characterize import characterize_top_mems_conf_with_openram
from chia.vlsi.sram_openram.openram_runner import OpenRAMConfig

char = characterize_top_mems_conf_with_openram(
    generated_src_files,                 # [(filename, contents)] with a .top.mems.conf inside
    OpenRAMConfig(),                     # sky130, 3 corners, layout on, DRC/LVS off, analytical timing
    cache_dir=None,                      # None = $CHIA_OPENRAM_CACHE_DIR on the worker, "" = no cache
    parallel=True,                       # one run_openram task per distinct macro, in parallel
    dispatch_options={"scheduling_strategy": "DEFAULT"},   # when called from inside a placement group
)
char.sram_libs        # [{"name": macro, "lib_contents": {corner: lib}, "lef_content": lef}] -> Hammer node
char.stub_files       # adapters + macro stubs -> assemble_generated_src_with_macros(...)
char.tile_specs       # specs with the geometry the MDF must describe (see Tiling)
char.srams[i].result  # OpenRAMResult: area_um2, access_time_ns, setup/hold, native collateral, from_cache, ...
```

`characterize_srams_with_openram` takes pre-parsed specs; `run_openram` is the
per-macro `@ChiaFunction(resources={"openram": 1})`.

MacroCompiler remap works exactly as for CACTI, with
`generate_openram_macrocompiler_lib(char.tile_specs, "openram_")`; the MDF
describes the adapter module `openram_<sram>` with Chipyard port names, and
the adapter instantiates the OpenRAM macro (active-low `csb`/`web`,
zero-extended `addr`/`din` because sky130 single-port macros carry a spare
row and column, spare-column write enable tied off, constant mask when the
macro is masked but the port is not).

## Configuration (`OpenRAMConfig`)

Everything has a sky130 default. The fields that change the macro are part of
the cache key; `timeout_seconds`, `openram_python`, `keep_temp`, `store_gds` are not.

- `corners`: chia `LibertyCorner`s (default ff/ss/tt as the CACTI flow) → one native `.lib` each.
- `analytical_delay=True` (SPICE characterization is hours per macro and needs ngspice, not in the image).
- `check_lvsdrc=False` (needs magic/netgen, not in the image). `netlist_only` is always False: without layout OpenRAM reports no area and writes no LEF.
- `route_supplies="ring"`, `perimeter_pins=True`: both are retried as `False` when OpenRAM's routers fail for a shape; the result records `supply_routed` / `perimeter_pins`.
- `max_depth=2048`, `max_width=None`: see Tiling.
- `extra_options={...}`: verbatim OpenRAM options; `config_template="..."`: text of an OpenRAM config file placed before the generated lines (the geometry/port/output lines always win).

Single-port sky130 macros need an even number of rows and columns *including*
the replica column and dummy row, so the runner adds a spare row and column
and flips the parity on OpenRAM's error if the guess was wrong.

## Tiling

OpenRAM/sky130 refuses macros deeper than 512 rows × 8-way column mux
("Number of words exceeds 2048"). A Chipyard SRAM beyond `max_depth`
(or `max_width`) is built as a smaller **tile** macro; the adapter and the MDF
entry carry the tile geometry and MacroCompiler composes the full SRAM from
copies of it (its normal job for vendor macro libraries). BOOM's 8192×256 L2
bank becomes four 2048×256 tiles.

## Cache

`run_openram` hashes the rendered OpenRAM config (geometry, ports, corners,
options) plus the OpenRAM version; a hit returns the stored collateral
instantly. The cache is a directory on the **worker** (`/scratch/openram_cache`
in the image; bind-mount a host path to keep it across container restarts).
ChiaFunctions: `prefill_openram_cache(mems_conf_or_specs, config)`,
`openram_cache_inventory()`, `export_openram_cache()` → bytes,
`import_openram_cache(bytes)`.

## Image

`dockerfiles/OpenRAMDockerfile` → `ghcr.io/ucb-bar/chia-openram`
(workflow `.github/workflows/openram.yml`, in `release-images.yml`). It carries a
pinned stable-branch OpenRAM checkout (the last PyPI release fails on several
BOOM shapes) with one upstream bug patched (GDS record lengths read as signed),
the sky130 PDK via ciel, the `sky130_fd_bd_sram` cell library installed with
OpenRAM's own `make sky130-install`, and OpenROAD for validating the collateral.

## Testing

- Unit tests: `pytest chia/vlsi/sram_openram/test` (hermetic, fixtures from a real macro).
- Local cluster: `cluster/openram_cluster.sh up`, `python cluster/openram_smoke_test.py`,
  or `cluster/openram_e2e.sh` (real OpenRAM runs + OpenROAD checks + cache round trip).
- Timing flow: `2_timingimprovement/improve_timing.py --sram-backend openram [--openram-cache-dir ...]`.
